title: Forge effect usage v1
description: Decision 0112 ruling 3: the optional, absent-by-default `usage` object on `effect/succeeded`, `effect/failed` and `effect/indeterminate`, published as a numbered extension at event_schema 1 under the amended rule in contracts/README.md. What the attempt's process tree used, as the engine measured it on its tracker's 100 ms tick from spawn to settlement (ruling 1): a single seat's measures, or several drivers' under `members`: a panel's, one entry per member a tick measured, or a sequence's, one entry per step driver a tick measured. An attempt no tick read carries none. Every field is a non-negative integer, so no seat-controlled text reaches the journal through it. `fold` reads none of it, RunState gains nothing, and nothing that settles, kills, retries or admits an attempt reads it (ruling 6).

members.description: Each driver's measures: a panel's keyed by the member's name, a sequence's by the tag its checkpoints ride under, `<step>` or `<step>:<member>`; a driver no tick measured is absent.

peak_memory_bytes.description: The highest summed resident set of the tree on any tick, in bytes: an upper estimate, since a shared page counts once per process.

mean_memory_bytes.description: That sum averaged over the attempt's ticks, in bytes: an upper estimate.

peak_load_millicores.description: The most cores the tree kept busy over a one-second window of ticks, in thousandths of a core; an attempt whose ticks span less than a second, its load since spawn.

mean_load_millicores.description: CPU time over wall time, in thousandths of a core.

cpu_ms.description: The tree's CPU time, user and system, the time of exited descendants its processes waited for included, in milliseconds.

wall_ms.description: The monotonic time from the driver's spawn to the attempt's settlement, in milliseconds.
